title: Everyday irregular verbs
description: Use the most common irregular verbs in the present: aller, faire, venir, prendre, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, connaître and more.

guide.summary: The verbs you use every day — aller, faire, venir, prendre, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, connaître, mettre, dire, voir, boire, lire, écrire — build their present on their own stems. Learn the six forms of each and you can say where you go, what you do, and what you can, want or must do.

sections.title: What stays regular
sections.text: Irregular verbs change their stem, but the endings are almost always the same ones. Learn the endings once; then only the stems are new.

rows: je vais, j’ai, je peux, je veux
vous êtes, vous faites, vous dites
ils vont, ils font, ils sont, ils ont

steps: Find the subject: who is doing it?
Take the verb’s stem for that person in its own table below.
Add the ending of that row, unless the verb is one of the exceptions.
watch: Only vous êtes, vous faites and vous dites end in -tes; everything else takes -ez (vous lisez, vous interdisez).
The -ent of ils is silent: ils viennent and il vient sound almost the same.
Many of these verbs share one form for je and tu: je peux / tu peux, je mets / tu mets.

sections.title: Aller: going somewhere
sections.text: Aller is the most irregular verb of all. Only nous and vous keep the all- stem of the infinitive; the other four forms start with v.
steps: Find the subject and take its row.
Ask whether it is nous or vous: those two keep all-, the rest start with v.
After aller, the place follows with à, au, à la or chez.

examples.fr: Tu vas à l’école à pied ?

watch: Alle, alles and allent do not exist: aller is not a regular -er verb.
Vont, font, sont and ont are the four short ils forms; they take no -ent.

sections.title: Faire: doing, making and the weather
sections.text: Faire covers both to do and to make, and it carries many fixed expressions. The weather is always il fait, never il est.
steps: Find the subject and take its row.
For the weather, use the impersonal il with faire: il fait beau, il fait froid, il fait chaud.
Learn the expressions as blocks: faire la cuisine, faire les courses, faire du sport.

examples.fr: Nous faisons la cuisine ce soir.
Mes sœurs font les courses le samedi.
examples.en: My sisters do the shopping on Saturdays.

watch: Faisez and faisent are invented forms; with vous the ending is -tes and the ils form is short.
Il est froid describes a thing or an unfriendly person, not the weather.

sections.title: Venir and prendre: the stem that doubles
sections.text: These two share one habit: nous and vous keep the quiet stem ven-/pren-, while ils/elles doubles the n. Their prefixed verbs follow exactly: revenir, devenir, apprendre, comprendre.
steps: Take off the prefix (re-, de-, ap-, com-), conjugate the base verb, then put the prefix back.
Singular: prendre keeps its d, venir uses the stem vien-.
Plural: nous and vous use ven-/pren-; ils and elles double the n and prendre loses its d.

examples.en: My son is getting very tall.

examples.fr: Elles prennent le train à huit heures.
examples.en: They take the train at eight.

watch: Prendent and prenent do not exist: no d, two n.
Il prend needs no extra -t: the d is already its ending.
Revienent and vienent are one n short of the plural stem.

sections.title: Pouvoir, vouloir, devoir: verb plus infinitive
sections.text: These three are followed directly by an infinitive, with no preposition in between. Each has three stems: one for the singular, one for nous/vous, one for ils/elles.
steps: Take the subject’s row of pouvoir, vouloir or devoir.
Check which of the three stems that row uses before writing the ending.
Put the infinitive straight after, with no à and no de: nous devons partir.

examples.en: We have to leave at noon.

watch: With je and tu, pouvoir and vouloir end in -x, not -s.
Peuvez, voulent as an ils form and devont mix two stems; read the row before writing.
The -t ending belongs to il, elle and on only: je dois, il doit.

sections.title: Savoir or connaître?
sections.text: Both mean to know. Savoir is for information and skills; connaître is for people, places and things you are familiar with.
steps: Look at what follows: an infinitive, or que, où, quand, pourquoi, si → savoir.
A person, a place or a thing standing alone → connaître.
Then take the subject’s row in that verb’s column.

examples.fr: Tu sais nager et tu connais bien la plage.
examples.en: You can swim and you know the beach well.

watch: Connaître is never followed by an infinitive or by que.
Savoir never takes a person or a city as its object.
The plural stem of connaître has a double s; the circumflex survives only in il connaît.

sections.title: Mettre, dire, voir
sections.text: All three keep a short singular and grow in the plural. Mettre also means to put on, for clothes.
steps: Take the subject’s row.
Singular: mettre has one t, voir keeps its i, and only il/elle/on ends in -t.
Plural: double the t of mettre, add s to dire, and turn the i of voir into y with -ons and -ez.

examples.fr: Je mets du sucre dans mon café.
examples.en: I put sugar in my coffee.

examples.fr: Nous voyons la mer de notre fenêtre.
examples.en: We see the sea from our window.

watch: Voyent does not exist: the y appears only with nous and vous.
Il met already ends in t: never il mets or il mett.
Vous dites breaks the -ez rule, but vous mettez and vous voyez do not.

sections.title: Boire, lire, écrire
sections.text: Each one hides a consonant that comes back in the plural: v for boire and écrire, s for lire. Boire takes yet another stem for ils/elles.
steps: Take the subject’s row.
Singular: short forms ending -s, -s, -t.
Plural: bring the hidden consonant back (buv-, lis-, écriv-), then check ils/elles, where boire changes stem again.

examples.fr: Les enfants boivent du lait le matin.
examples.en: The children drink milk in the morning.

examples.fr: Vous écrivez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
examples.en: You are writing a letter to your grandmother.

watch: Buv- stops at vous: it is not the ils stem.
Écrisez, écrient and lient are invented: keep the plural stem whole.

steps: Find the subject and take its row of aller.
Ask whether the subject is nous or vous: only those two keep the all- stem.
Never build aller like a regular -er verb.
Find the subject and take its row of faire.
Weather and expressions such as la cuisine, les courses or du sport use faire, not être.
With vous, remember faire is one of the three verbs that refuse -ez.
Take off any prefix (re-, de-, ap-, com-), conjugate the base verb, then put it back.
Decide singular or plural: the singular keeps the d of prendre and the vien- stem.
For ils/elles double the n and drop the d; for nous/vous use the quiet stem.
Take the subject’s row of pouvoir, vouloir or devoir.
Check which of the three stems that row uses: singular, nous/vous, or ils/elles.
Put the infinitive directly after the verb, with no preposition.
Read what follows the blank: an infinitive or a clause with que, où, quand calls for savoir.
A person, a place or a thing on its own calls for connaître.
Then take the subject’s row of the verb you chose.
Take the subject’s row.
Singular forms are short: one t in mettre, i in voir, and -t only for il/elle/on.
In the plural, use the long stem: mett-, dis-, voy- before -ons and -ez.
Take the subject’s row.
In the nous and vous forms, bring the hidden consonant back: buv-, lis-, écriv-.
Check ils/elles on its own line: boire does not keep the nous stem there.

exercises.hint: Aller is completely irregular with je. The form has three letters.
exercises.feedback: The je form of aller does not start with all-.
exercises.explanation: Aller in the present: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.

Vas is the tu form, for the person you are speaking to, not for yourself.
Va belongs to il, elle and on; with je the form ends in -s.
Vont is the ils/elles form, for several people.

exercises.hint: The subject is nous. Only the nous and vous forms of aller keep the all- stem.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous: the nous form of most verbs ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous allons: the nous form of aller keeps the regular-looking stem all- and ends in -ons.

mistakes.why: Allez is the vous form, the people you are speaking to. The subject here is we.

That is the infinitive, the dictionary form. After a subject the verb must be conjugated.

exercises.source: Mes parents ____ au marché le samedi.

exercises.hint: This is one of only three vous forms that do not end in -ez.
exercises.feedback: Faire does not use -ez with vous.
exercises.explanation: Vous faites, like vous êtes and vous dites, is an irregular vous form ending in -tes.

mistakes.why: Faisez applies the ordinary -ez ending, but faire is one of the three verbs that refuse it with vous.
Fais is the je/tu form, for one person.
Faisons goes with nous, the group you belong to.
Font is the ils/elles form, the people you are talking about.

exercises.hint: The nous form of faire is built on the stem fais-.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous. The nous form ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous faisons la cuisine: faisons is the nous form of faire, and faire la cuisine means to cook.

mistakes.why: Faisez does not exist, and -ez belongs to vous anyway; the subject here is we.
Font is the ils/elles form, for other people.
Fait is the il/elle/on form, one person. A plural subject needs a plural ending.

exercises.hint: French talks about the weather with il and the verb faire.
exercises.feedback: The weather expression uses faire, not être: il ____ beau.
exercises.explanation: Il fait beau means the weather is nice. Weather expressions use il fait.

mistakes.why: Est is être. French does not describe the weather with être.
Font is the ils/elles plural; the il of a weather sentence is a single impersonal subject.
Fais is the je/tu form; with il the ending is -t.

alternatives.message: Il est froid describes a thing or a person who is cold (unfriendly). For the weather, French says il fait froid.

exercises.hint: Weather in French uses il plus a form of faire.
exercises.feedback: Do not use il est for the weather. French uses another verb.
exercises.explanation: Il fait froid: the weather uses il fait, not il est.

The verb is left in the infinitive; after il it must be conjugated.

exercises.source: Qu’est-ce que vous faisez ce week-end ?
answers: Qu’est-ce que vous faites ce week-end ?
exercises.hint: The vous form of faire is one of the rare vous forms without -ez.
exercises.feedback: Faisez does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Vous faites is the correct vous form of faire.

answers: Qu’est-ce que vous faisez ce week-end ?
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: faisez uses the regular -ez ending, which faire refuses with vous.

answers: Qu’est-ce que vous faisons ce week-end ?

answers: Qu’est-ce que vous fait ce week-end ?

exercises.source: My sisters do the shopping on Saturdays.
answers: Mes sœurs font les courses le samedi.
exercises.hint: Mes sœurs means they. Pick the ils form of faire.
exercises.feedback: One tile looks like a regular form but does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Mes sœurs font les courses: font is the ils form of faire. Faire les courses means to do the shopping.

answers: Mes sœurs faisent les courses le samedi.
mistakes.why: Faisent is a made-up regular form. Faire has a short irregular plural with no -ent ending.

exercises.source: Je fais du sport le lundi.
answers: Nous faisons du sport le lundi.
exercises.hint: Only the verb changes. The nous form of faire uses the stem fais-.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending that goes with nous.
exercises.explanation: Je fais becomes nous faisons. The rest of the sentence stays the same.

answers: Nous fais du sport le lundi.
mistakes.why: Fais is the je form: the verb was left as it was when the subject changed.

answers: Nous faisez du sport le lundi.
mistakes.why: Faisez is not a French form, and -ez belongs to vous, not to a we.

answers: Nous font du sport le lundi.
mistakes.why: Font goes with ils and elles, people you talk about.

exercises.hint: The ils form of venir has the stem vienn- with a double n.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of venir changes its stem, like tu viens and il vient.
exercises.explanation: Ils viennent: the stem becomes vienn- (double n) before the silent -ent ending.

mistakes.why: One n is missing: the third-person plural stem doubles it before the silent ending.

Vient is the singular il/elle form, for one person.
Viens goes with je and tu.

exercises.source: Elles ____ le train à huit heures.
exercises.hint: The ils/elles form of prendre doubles one letter.
exercises.feedback: Look at the stem: the ils form of prendre has no d and a double n.
exercises.explanation: Elles prennent: prendre drops its d and doubles the n in the ils/elles form.

mistakes.why: Only one n here: the third-person plural stem doubles it.
The d survives only in the singular; the plural stem drops it.
Prend is the singular il/elle form, and elles is several people.

exercises.hint: Comprendre is conjugated like prendre. Think of tu prends.
exercises.feedback: Tu needs the -s ending, and comprendre keeps its d in the singular.
exercises.explanation: Tu comprends: like tu prends, the singular forms keep the d and tu ends in -s.

mistakes.why: Comprend is the il/elle/on form; with tu the verb takes an -s.
Comprenons goes with nous.
That is the ils/elles form, with the doubled n of the plural stem.

exercises.hint: Devenir is conjugated like venir. Think of il vient.
exercises.feedback: Mon fils means il. The il form of venir is vient.
exercises.explanation: Il devient, like il vient: the singular forms use the stem vien- and il ends in -t.

mistakes.why: Deviens is the je/tu form. Mon fils is a he, so the ending is -t.
The doubled n marks the plural, but mon fils is one person.
That is plain venir. The sentence asks for devenir, which keeps its de- prefix.
Devenir follows venir, whose singular stem is not the infinitive stem.

exercises.source: Mes amis revienent de Rome demain.

exercises.hint: Apprendre is conjugated like prendre. Languages take le or l’ in French.
exercises.feedback: Check the nous form of apprendre: it has no d.

mistakes.why: The d disappears in the plural, so the verb is not built on apprend- here.

Apprend is the il/elle form, one person; the subject is we.

exercises.instruction: Make the subject plural. Keep the rest the same.

Disons is the nous form.
Disent is the ils/elles form, with its silent ending.
Dis is the je/tu form, for one person.

exercises.source: Je ____ du sucre dans mon café.
exercises.hint: The singular forms of mettre have only one t. Je ends in -s.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to je: the je form ends in -s, and the double t appears only in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Je mets: mettre has one t in the singular (je mets, tu mets, il met) and two in the plural (nous mettons).

mistakes.why: Met is the il/elle/on form; with je the verb needs an -s.
The double t belongs to the plural, and -es is not a present ending of mettre.
Mettons goes with nous.

exercises.source: Ils voyent leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
answers: Ils voient leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
exercises.hint: Voir uses y only in the nous and vous forms.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of voir keeps the i.
exercises.explanation: Ils voient: the y appears only in nous voyons and vous voyez.

answers: Ils voyent leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the y belongs to the nous and vous forms only.

answers: Ils voit leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
mistakes.why: Voit is the singular il/elle form, but ils is plural.

answers: Ils voyons leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
mistakes.why: Voyons is the nous form, the group the speaker belongs to.

exercises.source: Nous ____ la mer de notre fenêtre.
exercises.hint: With nous, voir changes its i to y.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous. The ending is -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous voyons: the nous and vous forms of voir use y (voyons, voyez).

mistakes.why: The i turns into y before the endings -ons and -ez, so this spelling does not exist.
Voyez is the vous form, the people you are speaking to.
Voient is the ils/elles form, other people; the subject here is we.

exercises.hint: Mettre means to put on for clothes. Manteau is masculine.
exercises.feedback: Check the il/elle form of mettre: one t.
exercises.explanation: Elle met son manteau: the singular forms of mettre have one t (je mets, il met).

mistakes.why: Mets is the je/tu form; the il/elle form has no -s.
Mettes is not a present form: the singular keeps one t and takes no -es.
Manteau is masculine, so it takes the masculine possessive.
Porter means to wear, a state. The exercise asks for the action of putting the coat on.

exercises.source: I am seeing my friends this evening.
answers: Je vois mes amis ce soir.
exercises.hint: Choose the je form of voir.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the il form. Je needs a form ending in -s.
exercises.explanation: Je vois mes amis: voir with je ends in -s. The present is used for a planned evening too.

answers: Je voit mes amis ce soir.
mistakes.why: Voit is the il/elle form. With je the verb ends in -s.

exercises.hint: In the plural, écrire adds a v to its stem.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of écrire is not écrient.
exercises.explanation: Ils écrivent: the plural stem of écrire is écriv- (nous écrivons, vous écrivez, ils écrivent).

mistakes.why: That drops the consonant the plural stem adds; écrire is longer in the plural.
Écrit is the singular il/elle form, for one person.
Écrivons goes with nous.
Écris is the je/tu form.

exercises.source: Les enfants ____ du lait le matin.
exercises.hint: The ils form of boire uses the stem boiv-.
exercises.feedback: Buv- is only for nous and vous.
exercises.explanation: Ils boivent: boire uses buv- for nous and vous but boiv- for ils.

mistakes.why: Buv- is the stem of the nous and vous forms only; it stops at vous.
The v of the third-person plural stem is missing here.
Boit is the singular il/elle form, and les enfants is plural.

exercises.hint: The singular forms of lire are short. Tu ends in -s.
exercises.feedback: Tu needs the -s ending.
exercises.explanation: Tu lis: the singular of lire is je lis, tu lis, il lit.

mistakes.why: Lit is the il/elle/on form; with tu the verb ends in -s.
Lire is not a regular -er verb, so -es is not its tu ending.
Lisez is the vous form, polite or plural.
That is the infinitive; after tu the verb must be conjugated.

exercises.instruction: Make the subject plural. Keep the rest the same.
exercises.hint: Il becomes ils. The plural of lire adds an s to the stem.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of lire is not lient.
exercises.explanation: Ils lisent: the plural stem of lire is lis- (nous lisons, vous lisez, ils lisent).

mistakes.why: Only the subject was made plural; the verb is still the singular form.
That adds -ent to the short singular stem, but the plural stem of lire is longer.
Lisez belongs to vous, not to the people you are talking about.

exercises.source: Vous écrisez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
answers: Vous écrivez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
exercises.hint: The plural forms of écrire have a v in the stem.
exercises.feedback: Écrisez does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Vous écrivez: the plural stem of écrire is écriv-.

answers: Vous écrisez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the plural stem of écrire has a v, not an s.

answers: Vous écrivons une lettre à votre grand-mère.
mistakes.why: Écrivons is the nous form; the subject is vous.

answers: Vous écrivent une lettre à votre grand-mère.
mistakes.why: Écrivent is the ils/elles form, the people you are talking about.

exercises.hint: Use boire with je, and de l’ for some water.
exercises.feedback: Check the je form of boire: it has oi.
exercises.explanation: Je bois de l’eau: je bois, and de l’eau for an unspecified amount of water.

mistakes.why: Boit is the il/elle form; with je the verb ends in -s.
Buv- is the stem of nous and vous; the singular uses the oi stem.
L’eau means the water, one particular water. Drinking an unspecified amount needs a partitive article.
Du cannot stand before a vowel: the partitive changes shape there.

exercises.source: She writes a message to her brother.
answers: Elle écrit un message à son frère.
exercises.hint: Elle is singular. The singular of écrire has no v.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the plural form.
exercises.explanation: Elle écrit: the singular forms of écrire are écris, écris, écrit.

answers: Elle écrivent un message à son frère.
mistakes.why: Écrivent is the ils/elles form, but the subject tile is one person.
